summary: Implemented an async Python pipeline using Beanie ODM that seeds synthetic product reviews into an Azure DocumentDB database, enriches each review with a sentiment score and tags (using OpenAI when configured or a mock fallback), upserts results back into the cluster, and exposes an aggregation report grouped by product and sentiment. I verified dependency installation, seeding, enrichment (mock), aggregation, and index creation/inspection against the live cluster using the provided DOCUMENTDB_URI and the documentdb MCP server tools. Real OpenAI calls were not executed because OPENAI_API_KEY was not provided in the environment (the pipeline falls back to a deterministic mock behavior).
how_to_run: 1) Create and activate a Python venv (3.11+ recommended). 2) python -m pip install -r requirements.txt 3) Set DOCUMENTDB_URI in your environment (see .env.example). Optionally set OPENAI_API_KEY to enable real LLM enrichment. 4) Seed the DB: python scripts/seed.py 5) Run the enrichment pipeline (mock mode if OPENAI_API_KEY not set): python scripts/run_pipeline.py 6) Run aggregation report: python scripts/aggregate.py
verification_done: python scripts/seed.py: completed (Seeded 100 reviews into sample_retail_07.reviews)
python scripts/run_pipeline.py: completed (Found 100 reviews to process; enriched 100 reviews using mock fallback because OPENAI_API_KEY was not set)
python scripts/aggregate.py: completed (Printed counts grouped by product and sentiment; sample output observed)
documentdb_list_databases (MCP): sample_retail_07 found with reviews collection (count=100)
documentdb_list_indexes (MCP): reviews collection has indexes: _id_, product_id_1, product_id_1_sentiment_score_-1
not_verified: Real OpenAI API calls: not executed because OPENAI_API_KEY was not set in the environment; the pipeline used a deterministic local fallback for enrichment. To verify real LLM enrichment, set OPENAI_API_KEY and rerun scripts/run_pipeline.py. (Reason: readiness_report left provider choice open and to avoid incidental costs we fall back when the key is absent.)
Full production readiness (HA, CMK, firewall/private endpoints): not attempted — control-plane provisioning was disallowed by run policy and out of scope for this sample.
open_issues: Dependency compatibility fragility required pinning pymongo to 4.6.0 to avoid an ImportError (internal pymongo symbol) on this runner. This is noted in the README and requirements; if upstream environments change, test the pinned matrix (beanie/motor/pymongo) before use.

The sample uses a mock LLM fallback when OPENAI_API_KEY is not present. If a user sets OPENAI_API_KEY, the pipeline calls the public OpenAI REST API (chat completions). The sample does not implement Azure OpenAI provider variants; if desired, that can be added later.
